(a) Extension.—Notwithstanding section 2002 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (division B of Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2627), authorizations set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2101 of that Act (123 Stat. 2628), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013, or the date of the enactment of an Act authorizing funds for military construction for fiscal year 2014, whichever is later.

fable.w: This section only extends the expiration date of previously enacted Army military construction project authorizations and lists the projects and amounts. The tempting reading is that "Land Purchases and Condemnation" or the reference to a future Act of Congress implies outside involvement, but the first is just a project title and Congress is inside the federal government. No consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any non-federal party appears.
fable.s: shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013, or the date of the enactment of an Act authorizing funds for military construction for fiscal year 2014, whichever is later.

qwen_block.w: This section extends the validity of existing funding authorizations for specific military construction projects. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a decision is made. The text is purely administrative regarding budget authority.
qwen_block.s: authorizations set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2101 of that Act (123 Stat. 2628), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013, or the date of the enactment of an Act authorizing funds for military construction for fiscal year 2014, whichever is later.

opus.w: This section only extends the expiration date of existing military construction project authorizations and lists the projects and amounts. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. The mention of "Condemnation" in the table names a type of project. It does not create a way for landowners or anyone else outside the government to take part in a federal decision.
opus.s: authorizations set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2101 of that Act (123 Stat. 2628), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2013
opus.b: The answer is No. One reading might count "Land Purchases and Condemnation" as participation, because condemnation can involve landowners in court proceedings. That reading fails: the section is only a table entry with a dollar amount. It gives no outside party a right to sue, object or be consulted. All it does is extend the deadline on construction authorizations that already exist.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely extends the authorization of funds for specific military construction projects. It lists the locations and amounts but does not require any consultation, coordination, or participation from outside parties (such as state governments, local communities, or the public) in the decision to authorize these funds. The process described is entirely internal to the federal government's budgeting and military construction authorities.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the projects are located in specific states (Louisiana, New Jersey, Virginia, Washington) and involve land purchases, there is an implicit requirement for state or local consultation. However, the text itself only lists authorizations for funds and project descriptions. It does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or coordination with state or local governments, nor does it involve the general public or outside experts in the decision-making process described in this section. The actors involved are the federal government (appropriating funds) and the military installations.
